Why the Sports Industry Is Attractive for Private Equity
• One of the oldest and most deeply rooted forms of entertainment
• Fans spend on average ≈ $1,600 per year supporting their teams
• 46% of the world‘s population follows sport
• Increasing institutionalization and professionalization of ownership
• Multi-revenue model: Broadcasting rights, Sponsorship & commercial partnerships, Matchday revenues & Merchandising
• Sports assets show low correlation with public markets, providing diversification benefits in volatile macro environments (e.g. geopolitical shocks, pandemics)
• Fan engagement services growing even faster (20% YoY)
à Large, global, structurally resilient industry à Recurring, diversified and fast-growing revenue streams

The PE Value Creation Playbook in Sports
Four Core Levers Through Which Private Equity Drives Value Across Sports Assets

Private equity drives value in sports through revenue growth, operational improvements, digital transformation, and ecosystem expansion. The examples below highlight key value creation strategies used across sports investments:

• Growth through optimization of media rights, sponsorships, and commercial partnerships as well as premium ticket pricing, hospitality offerings, and global fan monetization • Global sports media rights valued at $62.6bn (2024) and forecast to exceed $78bn by 2030 • US market alone surged 122% over past decade

• Data analytics and performance technology improving player and team decisions • Centralized back-office, governance improvements, and professional management • For Example: Ajax AI system (in-house analytics), reduces scouting time by 70% and talent identification by 45%

• Development of streaming platforms and digital content distribution • DTC streaming platforms enabling clubs to own fan relationships and data • Sports betting partnerships creating new revenue streams • Fan engagement expected to grow 15-20% CAGR through 2028

• Multi-club ownership platforms creating scouting and talent synergies • Stadium-adjacent real estate and mixed-use districts (hotels, retail, entertainment) adding recurring, non-game-day cash flows to club P&Ls • MCO platforms: City Football Group (13 clubs), RedBird, FSG
Source(s): Apollo Global Management, Telecoming/Juniper Research (2024), Goldman Sachs, Houlihan Lokey

Inflation-linked contracts reset at higher rates at renewal. NFL with a $10B/yr comparable to Netflix's entire $16bn global content budget
Full/partial sale to media group or sports holding company at a valuation premium. CVC sale of F1 to Liberty Media for 4x return

Limited to franchise-holding companies. Growing for sports media and tech platforms (e.g. Manchester United NYSE listing, WWE/TKO)

Case Study: CVC Capital Partners × Formula One
The Quintessential PE Sports Investment – Transforming a Fragmented Racing Series into a $8bn Media & Entertainment Empire
CVC’S Value Creation Playbook at F1 (2006–2016)
Centralized broadcast rights globally, moving from national deals to a unified rights package marketed to premium networks and streamers.
Consolidated fragmented commercial rights under single entity; restructured team payment agreements to give F1 central commercial control.
Added Grands Prix in Abu Dhabi (2009), India (2011), Austin (2012). Today: 24-race calendar, ~4m fans at 14 mid-season races. F1 social following: 100m+, up 21% YoY.
Imposed cost caps and resource restriction agreements (RRAs) to improve team economics and reduce risk of competitive collapse. Attracted manufacturer investment.
→ Enabled unified media and sponsorship packaging
→ Revenue compounded at >8% p.a. during holding period
→ Hosting fees grew from ~$5m to $50m+ per race
→ Improved reliability and attractiveness for investors
CVC scaled Formula One into a global, media-driven platform through commercial centralization and expansion of the race calendar, demonstrating how
institutional ownership can unlock value in sports through improved governance and commercial execution
Source(s): Apollo Global Management (Dec 2025), Formula Rapida (Dec 2024), McKinsey Sports Investment Tracker, CVC Capital Partners

Financial Gains vs. Governance, Fan Relations & On-Field Performance

• PE cost optimization risks pricing out loyal core fan base • Frequent chairman and management changes destabilize club culture • League restrictions cap influence: NFL ≤10% per investor, 6-yr lockup • Majority stakes (Italy/France) enable restructuring; minority stakes (Spain/Germany) limit control

• Short-term roster and management turnover disrupts team chemistry • Revenue-first priorities can divert resources away from player development • PE return timelines misalign with the urgency of competitive seasons • Cost optimization pressures conflict with the investment needed to field a winning team

• No public market for sports stakes, making it illiquid, with narrow exit windows • 10% LTV vs. 40-70% in comparable asset classes shows structural underdeveloped • Financial gains concentrated in matchday and commercial revenue • Long holding periods due to operational value creation and limited exit liquidity
